title: IKEv2/IPsec: The VPN Built Into Your Phone
metaTitle: What Is IKEv2/IPsec? How It Works and Why It Is Easy to Block
metaDescription: IKEv2/IPsec explained: the built-in VPN on iPhone, Mac, Windows and Android, how MOBIKE keeps it connected on the move, and why fixed UDP ports 500 and 4500 make it easy to block.
excerpt: Built into iOS, macOS, Windows and Android, fast, and smooth when you switch networks. It runs on fixed, well-known ports, so blocking it takes one rule.

faq.question: What ports does IKEv2 use?
faq.answer: The key exchange uses UDP port 500. When a NAT router sits between the two sides, which is almost always the case, IKE and the encrypted traffic move to UDP port 4500.

faq.question: Why is IKEv2 good on phones?
faq.answer: The MOBIKE extension (RFC 4555) lets an IKEv2 connection survive a change of IP address, so moving from Wi-Fi to mobile data does not drop the tunnel.

faq.question: Is IKEv2 secure?
faq.answer: Yes, with current algorithms. It is an IETF standard used widely by enterprises. Its weakness is that it is easy to recognise and block, not that it is easy to decrypt.

faq.question: Does IKEv2 work in China or Russia?
faq.answer: It is generally unreliable on filtered networks, because blocking its fixed UDP ports or recognising its standard handshake is simple.
